tagline: Over Catawba Mountain and down the creek valleys to Paint Bank.
intro: Out of Hanging Rock, Route 311 leaves the Roanoke Valley along Mason Creek and climbs Catawba Mountain, crossing the Appalachian Trail on top. It drops into the Catawba valley, enters the Jefferson National Forest at McAfee Gap and follows Craig Creek to New Castle, the only town in Craig County. Then it climbs Potts Mountain and comes down to Paint Bank.

The other roads come in from the sides. Route 42 drops off Johns Creek Mountain into New Castle, and Route 43 follows the James River on Narrow Passage Road from Buchanan to Eagle Rock, where the road passes through a water gap between Rathole and Crawford mountains.

moments.title: McAfee Knob
moments.text: Four miles up the Appalachian Trail from Route 311, a ledge sticks out like a diving platform 1,600 feet above the Catawba Valley, reckoned the most photographed spot on the trail.

moments.title: Meadow Creek Falls
moments.text: Past the falls Route 42 turns twisty and descends between Sinking Creek and Johns Creek mountains, on a drop of 1,260 feet from Looney to New Castle.

moments.title: Paint Bank
moments.text: Named for the red clay in the banks of Potts Creek, once used for war paint and pottery, and known in the Civil War, for its mixed loyalties, as the Union Hole.
